title: Eventual Safe States
hints: a terminal node (no outgoing edges) is always safe - can you build up more safe nodes from there, working backwards?
reverse every edge; now a node is safe once every node it originally pointed to has already been confirmed safe

track each node's remaining out-degree in the original graph; when a node's out-degree drops to zero, it becomes safe - this is topological sort on the reversed graph, starting from the original sinks

seed a queue with all out-degree-zero nodes; when you mark a node safe, use the reverse adjacency list to decrement the out-degree of every node that originally pointed to it, enqueueing any that reach zero
sort the final list of safe node indices ascending before returning
commonMistakes: marking a node safe because just ONE outgoing path avoids a cycle, instead of requiring ALL of its paths to avoid cycles
not handling self-loops as an immediate cycle
running a single DFS coloring pass but forgetting to memoize results, leading to exponential blowup or incorrect state leaking between different starting nodes

content.problemStatement:
You're given a directed graph with `n` nodes, labeled 0 to n - 1, and a
list of directed edges, where each edge `[u, v]` means there is an edge
from node `u` to node `v`.

**Return every safe node's index, in ascending order.**

A node is "safe" if every possible path starting from it eventually reaches a terminal node (a node with no outgoing edges), no matter which outgoing edge is followed at each step. A node is unsafe if even one path from it can loop forever, whether it enters a cycle directly or leads into a node that is itself unsafe.
constraints: each edge [u, v] has 0 <= u, v < n
an edge may form a self-loop, i.e. u can equal v
notes: a graph with no edges at all - every node is safe
a node with a self-loop - that node is unsafe
a node with multiple outgoing edges where only some of them lead into a cycle - it's still unsafe, since EVERY path must be safe
the result can be an empty array when every node is unsafe

sampleTestCases.explanation: nodes 0, 1, 2 form a cycle, and node 3 leads into it; node 5 is terminal and node 4 only leads to node 5
with no edges at all, every node is already terminal, so every node is safe
node 2 has a self-loop (unsafe); node 0 has a path through node 2 into that cycle, so node 0 is unsafe too, even though its other path through node 1 is fine; node 4 has no edges at all
